messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — AcmeCorp on private deploy reporting a big spike in KMS decrypt errors after yesterday's keystore RBAC change. 500s in the agent logs, audit shows `denied:kms:Decrypt` for svcacc `model-serving`. Anyone seeing this?

sam: I picked up the alert at 22:30 UTC. linking logs: https://logs.internal/redwood/streams/keystore-proxy (perm:eng)

aisha: Can you paste a log snippet? curious if it's a 403 from KMS or our proxy denying.

maria: paste: ```
2026-03-22T22:28:11Z keystore-proxy[pod-abc] ERROR auth.go:142 deny: svcacc=model-serving action=Decrypt resource=projects/acme/keys/primary reason=rbac:binding-mismatch
2026-03-22T22:28:11Z keystore-proxy[pod-abc] WARN audit_id=0ab3fd path=/v1/decrypt status=403
```

ops-chris: that `rbac:binding-mismatch` matches the rolebinding we pushed in rollout-4721. deploy-bot shows the RBAC patch applied at 2026-03-22T21:54:02. devbot: see below.

devbot: deploy-bot: applied patch keystore-rolebinding v2 -> v3 (rollout-4721) by @infra@redwood (CI) at 2026-03-22 21:54:02 UTC

sam: I want to rule out networking: earlier we tightened netpols for keystore-agent egress to internal-kmscluster. If the proxy can't reach KMS it's usually conn errors not rbac denies, but worth checking `conntrack` and netpol logs. infra-monitor: any drops?

infra-monitor: We see denied-egress metrics increasing from keystore-proxy pods after the rollout window, but TCP handshake to kms.internal is succeeding for most requests. no large conntrack evictions found.

aisha: sounds like RBAC regression then. Suggest emergency mitigation: 1) roll back rolebinding to v2 2) in parallel add temporary allow rule for `model-serving` svcacc to kms:Decrypt for 1 hour while we debug 3) capture audit chain and evidence.

maria: agreed. Ops, can you do a rollback? we need to notify AcmeCorp SRE too. Also we should avoid mass key re-encryption — no crypto ops.

ops-chris: I can rollback the rolebinding in 10m. command I will run: ```kubectl apply -f /infra/rbac/keystore-rolebinding-v2.yaml -n priv-keystore``` Will post diff after.

sam: When you rollback, please also `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/keystore-proxy -n priv-keystore` to pickup policy cache clear. The proxy caches auth decisions for ~30s, but restart ensures clean state.

ops-chris: got it. doing rollback now.

ops-chris: rollback done at 22:38 UTC. diff: - subjects: svcacc:model-serving (removed) + subjects: svcacc:model-serving (added back with original binding to role:keystore-reader) (I Screenshotted the RBAC diff and uploaded to incident ticket).

maria: after rollback I'm still seeing a handful of 403s but dropping fast. Acme SRE confirms traffic returning to normal. :thumbsup:

aisha: follow-ups: - add deploy metadata (deploy_id) to keystore audit events for easier correlation - improve canary window for RBAC changes on private (30m with smoke checks) - add automated test that verifies svcacc token can call kms:Decrypt in staging before rollout

sam: Also consider a temporary audit-only mode for keystore-proxy where denials log full principals+bindings without enforcing, to surface mismatches during rollout. We can gate via a k8s feature flag.

maria: Good idea. For the postmortem: list of action items + owners. I'll open INC-20260322-A and assign. Keep updates in this thread.

infra-monitor: FYI: I've increased audit retention for priv-keystore logs by +72h for this incident.

ops-chris: Confirming: rollback + restart + monitor. I'll keep watch for 2h.

aisha: I'll draft the postmortem and include RBAC test case.

maria: thanks team. we should also add a short runbook bullet: "if keystore 403s spike after RBAC, rollback rolebinding, restart proxy, notify customer, keep audit logs". saving that here.

maria: tagging @oncall-sre for awareness and closing loop.
